items.quote:
This is hands-down the best co-op game of the year—and the most fun I’ve had since Exhibition 33! It nails everything: hilarious moments, real challenge, satisfying progression, and an incredible drop-in/drop-out co-op system that makes playing with friends effortless. 
Sure, there are a few glitches and frame drops, but they’re completely overshadowed by how insanely fun the gameplay is. The loot system is addictive, the combat is tight, and the social experience is unmatched. All my friends are playing it right now and loving every second—we’re not waiting around for perfection when the game is already this good. 
I’m not going to sit around waiting a year for patches just so one guy can run the game at native resolution like it’s 2010. It’s 2025—DLSS, FSR, and upscaling exist for a reason. Clinging to native like it’s some sacred benchmark is just numb at this point. Meanwhile, my buddy with a 6700XT is playing it flawlessly and having a blast. Unless your whole crew agrees to hit pause for a year (good luck with that) over one person’s resolution purity test, you’re missing out on the best co-op fun in ages.

Quality of life features all over the place, old systems being either buffed or retired for better ones...I've got to be honest, as a longtime fan of Gearbox and Borderlands, if you don't like this one or have so many complaints about it or whatever, you are never going to enjoy these games and this company the way that we do. Gearbox treats us better than so many other companies, the DLC is reasonably priced every single entry, no microtransactions, ffs you people make me wish they'd start locking you whiney morons out of games permenantly for making an immature scene of yourselves. Bugs aside, we got a more mature game, a better story than 3, there is going to be endless amounts of things to do, meaning the endgame of 4 is going to outlast even 3 which has a TON of content now that it is complete. You haters can say whatever you want, Pitchford is right, this is one of the best made games in the entire industry with actual love and care into it, great writing, great voice acting...there is so much that they get right that I will NEVER respect you people for flaming them about a somewhat rocky launch. Most of you DO NOT deserve Borderlands, and I wouldn't even mind if Gearbox starting taking it away from you/blocking you out of purchasing their art altogether. To Randy and everyone at Gearbox and even 2K for not ruining the game with overbearing publishing, THANK YOU I LOVE BORDERLANDS!
items.author: Read_a_book_ffs

items.quote:
The best gameplay, movement and gunplay of all Borderlands games so far. Haven't finished the story yet but it seems adequate and the open world should give it some replayability or longer life.

Borderlands 4 also runs much smoother than Borderlands 3 did on release. I run at 120-156fps (cap) on a 5070 Ti with 2x frame gen which feels responsive and good. The graphics are of course very good too since it is a UE5 game.
I haven't had any crashes so far so it seems stable too (18 hours in).

Just one warning, this game is very demanding in general and I recommend playing this on a good PC for a proper experience. Hopefully Gearbox can optimize the game a bit further so that more people can enjoy this excellent Borderlands experience.

EDIT: Completed the whole game and reached UVH5 now, everything was very smooth and I had zero crashes (68 hours playtime). The only bad thing I can say is that Borderlands 4 didn't have any memorable characters like 1, 2 and 3 did. The story is decent and the are some fun side-quests mixed in.
